html:
On 30 May 1969, called Trinta di Mei, a strike by workers at the Shell refinery in Curacao turned into a riot. Marchers burned much of the centre of Willemstad, and Dutch marines were flown in to restore order. Two people died.

Behind it lay low pay, unemployment and the dominance of white Dutch and local elites. Workers were inspired by the civil rights and Black Power movements in America.

The revolt changed island politics. Labour leaders entered parliament and Afro-Curacaoans took a larger part in government. It also pushed the use of Papiamento and Caribbean pride, and fed later moves toward self rule within the kingdom of the Netherlands.
